flags.issueFull: At 5v5 (v3.8, Command 8, Arrow Storm × 1.5) first-turn Command 5 and 8 played the same 1,000 games move for move: Brain 5 spends 4 to 5 Command on the first mover's first turn whatever it has (checked here on 6 seeds at × 1, × 1.5, × 2: 4 to 5.5 used). Without Storm, 297 of 1,000 games differ. So at 5v5 the study can't show what equal first-turn Command does: the bot doesn't use the extra (Bot minimum). Example: seed of 5v5-c8-ftc8-storm15 game 0, turn 1
flags.next: Recommended: before ruling F12 at 5v5, a brain setting that values first-turn moves (advance or warm up with the spare Command), or a 5v5 re-run under Brain 7. Missing setting, harder to prove than a useless one

flags.issueFull: Brief 014, v3.8 baseline (Brain 5 mirror, 1,000 games per format, same seeds as v3.7): 5v5 changed a lot, 7v7 didn't. At 5v5 the first mover's share of decisive games went from 3.2% to 58.0% (F39's collapse is gone), but games ending on the turn limit went from 35.1% to 61.9%, pull KOs from 44.0% to 23.5%, draws from 1.1% to 6.4%, and the first attack comes on turn 4.4 instead of 2.9. 7v7: every measure within 4 points. Likely the 2-ring deploy area and the 8-hex gap keep Arrow Storm out of early reach, but field and deploy radius changed together: likely, not isolated
flags.next: Recommended: merge v3.8 as the Editor locked it, then fold 5v5 v3.8 into the stall study (brief 016's follow-up) instead of tuning now. If the Editor wants the cause isolated first, one sim-only screen: v3.8 at 5v5 with deployRadius5 = 3 against v3.8, same seeds, 200 games per side. F39 can close if the Editor accepts the field as its fix

Measured in a headless phone browser on this build
flags.next: Recommended: draw the 5v5 field at 7v7's hex size (centred, a margin each side) instead of filling the width; its half becomes about 400 px and fits with room. It changes the 5v5 look, so it needs the Editor's go-ahead. Not built
